correctness.rationale: For the iid scalar reflected update x[k+1]=x[k]-hU[k](2x[k]-x[k-1]), independently reconstructed the three-moment transfer K on (E x[k]^2,E x[k-1]^2,E x[k]x[k-1]); its polynomial determinant det(I-K)=h(2m-hv-3h^2mv). K is the restriction of a PSD-cone-preserving covariance map. Perturbation of the simple eigenvalue 1 at h=0 has slope -2m; its Perron spectral radius cannot cross 1 before the unique positive root, and det(I-K)<0 above that root gives a real eigenvalue >1. PSD spectral eigenvectors decompose into deterministic pair initializations, proving the quantifier, including equality/instability. For independent Bernoulli slopes 0 and 2m at h=1/(2m), symbol word 0,1,0 annihilates every augmented pair and gives P(T>3k)<=(7/8)^k; the exact second-moment recurrence S[n+1]=S[n]+S[n-1]/2 for initial (0,1) grows at root (1+sqrt3)/2 despite almost-sure finite hitting, whereas SGD risk is 2^-n. Read the full Fraction verifier; checked its exact enumerated conditions against the analytic derivation, but did not treat reported VERIFY_OK as a universal proof.

value.rationale: A sharp necessary/sufficient stability frontier for the natural one-call stochastic reflected-gradient algorithm, dependent only on oracle mean/second moment and valid for every deterministic initial state, is a motivated rate-calibration fact. The explicit contrast between almost-sure exact finite hitting and exponentially divergent mean-square risk under the *same one-call oracle* reveals a nontrivial stability pitfall not explained by a routine scalar deterministic contraction.

limitations: Scalar independent random slope with v<infinity; not general multidimensional/noisy nonlinear or correlated-oracle systems.
